column4: The section's B001 dictionary reading of م ن ن as cutting or diminution is denied by غير ممنون here; 84:25 repeats the believing-doer exception after 84:24's warning of painful punishment.
The section's B001 root م ن ن names a reward that is not cut or reduced; 41:8 gives the same promise, لهم أجر غير ممنون, to believers who do good.
The section reads غير ممنون as an uncut reward; here the Prophet himself is promised أجر غير ممنون, making the same assurance personal to him.
The section's “not cut off” reward is restated for the blessed as عطاء غير مجذوذ, a gift that is not severed; the different wording confirms the same continuity.
The section's B003 dictionary sense of م ن ن is a favor made heavy by claiming it; this verse says spenders do not follow what they gave with منّ or harm, and places their reward with their Lord.
The section's B003 sense of م ن ن as reproachful favor appears in the command not to cancel charity with المن والأذى; the washed bare stone pictures a good act emptied by that treatment.

The section's B003 sense of م ن ن as claiming a favor appears when Bedouins boast their submission to the Prophet; the reply assigns the favor of guidance to God rather than the recipients of the boast.

The section notes م ن ن can name a benign favor as well as a burdensome one; Yusuf says مَنَّ الله علينا, then says God does not waste the reward of those who do good, joining divine favor to returned recompense.
The section connects أجر with good action and notes the root حسن in “best”; this verse says God does not waste the reward of one who أحسن عملا, directly joining recompense to excellent work.
The section connects أجر to the return for work and حسن to what is best; this verse promises people who do good their reward بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون.
The section's B001 dictionary sense of المنون is death that cuts a life short; the disbelievers wait for the Prophet to be struck by ريب المنون, the opposite of the uncut reward promised him in 68:3.

The section labels خَلاق, from root خ ل ق, as a share of good fortune; this verse says the person seeking only worldly life has no خلاق in the Hereafter, setting a boundary against the lasting share promised to believers.
The section describes fatigue as stopping a traveler on the way; 84:6 instead pictures a person كادح إلى ربه and then meeting Him, carrying effort through to encounter.
The section cites 84:6's labor toward meeting the Lord; the next scene begins with the person's record placed in the right hand, showing how that meeting proceeds for one whose account is favorable.
After 84:6's striving and meeting, this verse promises an easy reckoning; it gives the encounter a concrete outcome alongside the section's promised recompense.
This verse completes the favorable meeting sequence after 84:6: the person returns to his people joyfully, a lived outcome of the easy account in 84:8.
This verse's warning of painful punishment is the side of the boundary that 84:25 immediately excepts; its own contribution is to make the succeeding uncut reward a real exception.

The section says the descending line and exception recur in this surah; 103:2 states that humanity is in loss, while 103:3 supplies the exception, paralleling the section's mortal decline and saved group.
The section points to the exception after decline; 103:3 repeats إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ, then adds mutual counsel in truth and patience to the spared group.
The section cites this surah's exception pattern: 70:19 describes humanity as created anxious, and the following verses define the worshippers excepted from that condition.
The section invokes the exception pattern; إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ begins the answer to 70:19's general human condition, as 95:6 sets believers and doers apart from the descent in 95:5.
This verse specifies the excepted worshippers as constant in prayer, showing a sustained practice behind the section's emphasis on intentional good deeds.

Among the traits of those excepted in 70:22, this verse calls wealth a known right; treating it as a due rather than a favor claimed from someone clarifies the section's reading of a reward free of burdensome minnah.
This verse names the recipients of the known right in 70:24, the asker and deprived; it completes that giving scene and distinguishes a due from a favor that can be held over them.
The section says belief in the Day of Judgment is the precise opposite of 95:7's challenge; 70:26 names those who يصدقون بيوم الدين, making that contrast explicit.

The section's secondary sense of م ن ن includes harm attached to a gift; 2:263 says kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, clarifying that the recipient's treatment matters alongside the act.

After 2:264's charity erased by reproach, this verse depicts spending for God's approval as a garden that yields twice its produce; its own image supplies the fruitful counterpart to giving that is emptied.
The section hears “not burdened by minnah” as a payment that makes no claim on its recipient; the righteous here say they feed others seeking God's face and want no reward or thanks from them.

The section's B001 dictionary sense of م ن ن includes fatigue that stops a traveler; here traveler's نصب in God's cause is recorded as a good deed, and God does not waste the reward of those who do good.

The section defines recompense as what comes back for an act; continuing 9:120's journey scene, this verse records each small or large expenditure and each valley crossed so God can repay the best of their deeds.
The section contrasts a life that ends with a reward not cut off; this verse says what people possess will perish while what is with God remains, then promises patient people their reward.

The section's B001 fatigue sense of م ن ن is a wearied traveler cut off from movement; here the eternal home granted by God's bounty has no نصب or لغوب, removing both fatigue and weariness from the lasting abode.
The section says fatigue can sever a walk; in the Garden described here no نصب touches its people and they are not expelled, joining freedom from weariness to remaining there.
The section's reward cannot be cut off; here those who recite, pray, and spend hope in a trade لن تبور, a transaction that will not perish, giving a concrete parallel for an enduring return.
Completing 35:29's nonperishing trade, this verse says God will pay their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty, directly extending the section's uncut recompense.
The section glosses غير ممنون as neither cut nor diminished; this verse says God does not wrong an atom's weight, and multiplies a good deed, adding full justice and increase to that promise.
The section's dictionary definition makes أجر what returns for a deed; this passage begins that sequence by saying a person has only what he strives for, connecting the recompense to his own effort.
Continuing 53:39's account of striving, this verse says the effort will be seen; it gives the deed a recognized place before the recompense in 53:41.
This verse completes 53:39-40 by saying the striving is then repaid with the fullest recompense, a direct formulation of the section's deed returning as reward.

The section says death can cut a life but not the believer's promised wage; this verse says those killed in God's way are alive with their Lord and provided for, making death no endpoint for their provision.
Continuing the martyrs' scene in 3:169, this verse shows them rejoicing in God's bounty and without fear for those not yet joined them, giving the post-death provision a continuing horizon.
This verse completes the martyrs' sequence with glad tidings of bounty and the statement that God does not waste the believers' reward, directly answering the section's concern that death end a wage.
The section says the promised reward is not diminished; in this verse God joins believing descendants to their families without depriving the believers of anything from their deeds.

The section describes a downward human line ending with life's exhaustion; this verse stages human development through old age, when some are returned to أرذل العمر, and places that decline beside resurrection.
This verse describes people being taken in death or returned to أرذل العمر until knowledge fades, a concrete bodily decline that illuminates the section's descending human condition.
The section moves from the best human form to the lowest; this verse traces a person's weakness to strength and back to weakness and gray age, giving that reversal a bodily sequence.
The section ends by challenging denial of recompense; 82:6 similarly asks what has deceived the human being about his generous Lord, setting up the creation and denial sequence in 82:7-9.
The section names خ ل ق in the claim that God created humanity in the best form; 82:7 says God created, proportioned, and balanced the human, a close creation scene before 82:9's denial of judgment.
This verse continues 82:7's account of the fashioned human by saying God composed him in whatever form He willed, extending the creation scene tied to the section's 95:4.
After 82:7-8 describe the fashioned human, this verse says بل تكذبون بالدين; that sequence joins the section's best-form creation in 95:4 to its challenge about denying the Judgment in 95:7.
The section contrasts a worldly return with an afterlife share; this verse names people who prefer الحياة الدنيا, setting up the next verse's more lasting Hereafter.
This verse completes the contrast in 87:16 by calling the Hereafter خير وأبقى, a specific statement of the lasting value that helps explain the section's uncut reward.

This verse identifies the disbelievers as deniers before 84:24's warning and 84:25's exception; its own contribution is the opposing stance to the believing group whose uncut reward the section cites.

The section defines أجر as the return for a good act; in the same charity passage as 2:262-64, 2:261 pictures spending for God multiplying like grain with seven ears, making abundance a concrete form of returned reward.

The section reads a reward free of minnah as one that does not burden its recipient; this verse says spending is for God's face and will be repaid fully without wrong, joining unclaimed giving to complete recompense.
The section's dictionary definition of أجر allows recompense in this life or the next; 4:134 states that both kinds of reward are with God, making that twofold scope explicit.

The section's B003 dictionary note on حسن connects doing good with the best and more as reward; this verse says those who do good have al-husna and ziyada, extending the reward beyond the deed's return.
The section moves from humanity's best form to a downward line; this verse says long life can reverse a person in creation, ننكسه في الخلق, giving that decline a direct bodily formulation.

The section promises a wage that is not diminished; amid migration, hardship, fighting, and death, this verse says God will not let any worker's work be lost, tying costly actions to preserved recompense.
The section denies that reward is cut or reduced; this verse promises the patient a reward without account, adding the distinct idea of a return beyond ordinary reckoning.
